column22: Robots spent large portions of the experiments in corners, along walls, and bunched up with other robots. During these periods, faulty robots behave very similarly, if not identically, to normal robots. It is only during the relatively uncommon moments when robots are isolated that the observer can clearly differentiate between faulty and normal behaviors. It seems the robots in the swarm suffered from this issue just as I did; the swarm identified many false positive faults when robots were bunched up or in corners.
column23: The robots’ behaviors were dynamic and unpredictable. It was rather difficult to focus on individual robot behaviors since many robots were present and moving around. Robot behavior was often manipulated by other robot behaviors, such as robots hitting walls not due to the fault of their own sensors, but due to the presence of other robots. In this case, context is important but is difficult to derive due to so many things happening at once
